cases.sentence: Мой ___ был тоже ни на одного из них не похож и составлял мое редкое исключение.
cases.translation: My friend, too, resembled none of them and was my rare exception.
cases.explain: «Друг» is the subject of the verb «был» (was), taking the nominative case.

cases.sentence: На приход мой ни один из них не обратил почти никакого ___.
cases.translation: Not one of them paid almost any attention to my arrival.
cases.explain: The negated verb phrase «не обратил... внимания» takes the genitive case (genitive of negation).

cases.sentence: Зверкову он доводился к каким-то дальним ___.
cases.translation: He was some kind of distant relative of Zverkov's.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» governs the dative case: «к родственникам» = 'related to relatives.'

cases.sentence: Вот этому-то уезжавшему Зверкову и хотели дать ___ наши товарищи.
cases.translation: It was for this departing Zverkov that our comrades wanted to give a dinner.
cases.explain: «Обед» is the direct object of the verb «дать» (to give), requiring the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Симонов провожал меня до передней с суетливым ___, который ему вовсе не шел.
cases.translation: Simonov saw me to the entryway with a fussy air that didn't suit him at all.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» governs the instrumental case: «с видом» = 'with an air.'

cases.sentence: Видел я его тоже один раз в ___ в третьем ярусе уже в аксельбантах.
cases.translation: I also once saw him at the theater, in the third tier, already wearing aiguillettes.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» governs the prepositional case: «в театре» = 'at the theater.'

reading.ru: Я застал у него еще двух моих школьных товарищей.
reading.question: Whom did the narrator find at Simonov's when he arrived?
options: Two more of his old schoolmates
reading.correct: Two more of his old schoolmates
reading.explain: He says he found two more of his old schoolmates at Simonov's.

reading.ru: Я, конечно, понимал, что они должны были презирать меня теперь за неуспех моей служебной карьеры и за то, что я уж очень опустился, ходил в дурном платье и прочее, что в их глазах составляло вывеску моей неспособности и мелкого значения.
reading.question: Why does the narrator think his old schoolmates must despise him now?
options: His failed career and shabby clothes, which signaled his incompetence and insignificance
His refusal to attend school reunions
reading.correct: His failed career and shabby clothes, which signaled his incompetence and insignificance
reading.explain: He understands they must despise him for his failed career and shabby clothing, signs of incompetence in their eyes.

reading.ru: Шла речь серьезная и даже горячая о прощальном обеде, который хотели устроить эти господа завтра же, сообща отъезжавшему далеко в губернию их товарищу Зверкову, служившему офицером.
reading.question: What were the gentlemen discussing so heatedly when the narrator arrived?
options: A farewell dinner for their friend Zverkov, an officer leaving for the provinces
reading.correct: A farewell dinner for their friend Zverkov, an officer leaving for the provinces
reading.explain: They were seriously discussing a farewell dinner for their comrade Zverkov, an officer departing for the provinces.

reading.ru: В низших классах он был только хорошенький, резвый мальчик, которого все любили.
reading.question: How was Zverkov described as a boy in the lower school grades?
options: A pretty, lively boy whom everyone loved
A cruel bully feared by all
reading.correct: A pretty, lively boy whom everyone loved
reading.explain: In the lower grades he was only a pretty, lively boy whom everyone loved.

reading.ru: В последний год его в нашей школе к нему досталось наследство 200 душ, а так как у нас все почти были бедны, то он даже перед нами стал фанфаронить.
reading.question: What windfall did Zverkov receive in his last year at school, prompting him to boast?
reading.correct: An inheritance of 200 serfs ("souls")
reading.explain: In his last school year he inherited 200 souls, and began to boast in front of his poorer classmates.

reading.ru: Я ненавидел его красивое, но глупенькое лицо, на котором я бы, впрочем, променялся охотой свое умное.
reading.question: What did the narrator admit he would have willingly traded his own "intelligent" face for?
reading.correct: Zverkov's handsome but silly face
reading.explain: He hated Zverkov's handsome but silly face, which he admits he would gladly have traded his own clever one for.

reading.ru: И наши хамы аплодировали.
reading.question: How did the other schoolmates react to Zverkov's boast about the "droit de seigneur"?
reading.correct: They applauded him
reading.explain: The text says 'and our louts applauded.'

reading.ru: На улице он мне уже не кланялся, и я подозревал, что он боится компрометировать себя, раскланиваясь с такой незначительной, как я, личностью.
reading.question: What did the narrator suspect once Zverkov stopped greeting him on the street?
options: That Zverkov feared compromising himself by acknowledging so insignificant a person
That Zverkov had forgotten his face
That Zverkov had left the city
reading.correct: That Zverkov feared compromising himself by acknowledging so insignificant a person
reading.explain: He suspected Zverkov feared compromising himself by bowing to such an insignificant person as himself.

reading.ru: Я уверен в этом.
reading.question: What is the narrator certain of, regarding his old schoolmates and Zverkov?
options: That they never truly considered themselves his equals
That Zverkov would never become an officer
reading.correct: That they never truly considered themselves his equals
reading.explain: He says he's sure that although they kept company with Zverkov for three years, they never inwardly considered themselves on equal footing with him.

reading.ru: Меня он постоянно считал ни во что, обращался, уже хоть не совсем вежливо, но сносно.
reading.question: How did Trudolyubov generally treat the narrator?
options: He considered him worthless but treated him tolerably, if not quite politely
He was openly cruel and violent
reading.correct: He considered him worthless but treated him tolerably, if not quite politely
reading.explain: Trudolyubov always regarded him as nothing much, but treated him tolerably, if not entirely politely.

reading.ru: завтра в пять часов», — окончательно заключил Симонов, которого выбрали распорядителем.
reading.question: Who was chosen to be the organizer of the farewell dinner?
reading.correct: Simonov
reading.explain: The text says Simonov was chosen as the one to make arrangements.

reading.ru: Он знал меня наизусть.
reading.question: What phrase does the narrator use to describe how well Simonov understood him?
reading.correct: Simonov knew him "by heart"
reading.explain: He says, 'He knew me by heart.'

reading.ru: «Мне кажется, об этом никто не вправе судить», — возразил я с дрожью в голосе.
reading.question: How did the narrator respond, with a trembling voice, when accused of previously being on bad terms with Zverkov?
options: He said no one had the right to judge that
reading.correct: He said no one had the right to judge that
reading.explain: He objected with a trembling voice that no one had any right to judge that.

reading.ru: «Завтра в пять часов в отель Де Пари, не ошибитесь».
reading.question: What final instruction does Simonov give about the dinner?
options: Tomorrow at five o'clock at the Hôtel de Paris, don't be mistaken
Arrive early to help set up
reading.correct: Tomorrow at five o'clock at the Hôtel de Paris, don't be mistaken
reading.explain: Simonov says, 'Tomorrow at five o'clock at the Hôtel de Paris, don't be mistaken.'

reading.ru: Симонов, с которым я остался с глазу на глаз, был в каком-то досадливом недоумении и странно посмотрел на меня.
reading.question: How did Simonov look at the narrator once they were left alone together?
reading.correct: With vexed bewilderment, strangely
reading.explain: Left alone with the narrator, Simonov was in some vexed bewilderment and looked at him strangely.

reading.ru: Я вспыхнул, но вспыхивая, вспомнил, что с незапамятных времен должен был Симонову 15 рублей, чего, впрочем, и не забывал никогда, но и не отдавал никогда.
reading.question: What debt did the narrator suddenly remember owing Simonov?
reading.correct: 15 rubles, owed from time immemorial
reading.explain: He flushed, remembering he had owed Simonov 15 rubles since time immemorial, never forgotten but never repaid.

reading.ru: — повторял Симонов, провожая меня до передней с суетливым видом, который ему вовсе не шел.
reading.question: How did Simonov behave while seeing the narrator to the door?
options: With a fussy manner that didn't suit him at all
reading.correct: With a fussy manner that didn't suit him at all
reading.explain: Simonov saw him to the entryway with a fussy manner that didn't suit him at all.

reading.ru: Но из них 7 надо было дать завтра же месячного жалования Аполлону, моему слуге, который жил у меня за 7 рублей на своих харчах.
reading.question: What did the narrator need to pay his servant Apollon the next day?
reading.correct: 7 rubles of monthly wages
reading.explain: Of his 9 rubles, 7 had to go the next day toward Apollon's monthly wages.

reading.ru: Они цинически смеялись над моим лицом, над моей мешковатой фигурой.
reading.question: What did his schoolmates cynically mock about the narrator?
options: His face and his baggy figure
reading.correct: His face and his baggy figure
reading.explain: They cynically laughed at his face and his baggy figure.

reading.ru: Конечно, много тут было от глупости, от дурного примера, беспрерывно окружавшего их детство и отрочество.
reading.question: What does the narrator attribute much of his schoolmates' bad behavior to?
options: Stupidity and the bad example that constantly surrounded their childhood and adolescence
reading.correct: Stupidity and the bad example that constantly surrounded their childhood and adolescence
reading.explain: He attributes much of it to stupidity and the bad example that continually surrounded their childhood and youth.

reading.ru: Дико и насмешливо смотрели они на это, но нравственно подчинялись, тем более, что даже учителя обращали на меня внимание по этому поводу.
reading.question: How did the schoolmates react once even the teachers began paying attention to the narrator?
options: They looked on wildly and mockingly, yet morally submitted
They expelled him from their group entirely
reading.correct: They looked on wildly and mockingly, yet morally submitted
reading.explain: They looked at it wildly and mockingly, but morally submitted, especially once the teachers noticed him for it.

reading.ru: Первым делом моим по выходе из школы было оставить ту специальную службу, которой я предназначался, чтобы все нити порвать, проклясть прошлое и прахом его посыпать.
reading.question: What was the narrator's first act upon leaving school?
options: Abandoning the special career track he was destined for, to cut all ties with the past
reading.correct: Abandoning the special career track he was destined for, to cut all ties with the past
reading.explain: His first act upon leaving school was to abandon the special service he was destined for, to sever every tie with the past.

reading.ru: Я предчувствовал, что одно уже это пятно отнимет у меня девять десятых собственного достоинства.
reading.question: What did the narrator fear a single stain on his trousers would cost him?
reading.correct: Nine-tenths of his own self-respect/dignity
reading.explain: He sensed this single stain would take away nine-tenths of his own dignity.

reading.ru: Мало того, в самом сильнейшем пароксизме трусливой лихорадки мне мечталось держать верх, победить, увлечь, заставить их полюбить себя, но хоть за возвышенность мысли и несомненное остроумие.
reading.question: Even in his feverish fear, what did the narrator dream of achieving at the dinner?
options: Gaining the upper hand and making them love him for his lofty thoughts and wit
reading.correct: Gaining the upper hand and making them love him for his lofty thoughts and wit
reading.explain: Even amid his feverish cowardice, he dreamed of gaining the upper hand and making them love him for his loftiness of thought and undoubted wit.

reading.ru: В невыразимой тоске я подходил к окну, отворял форточку и вглядывался в мудную мглу густо падающего мокрого снега.
reading.question: What did the narrator do in his inexpressible anguish while waiting for the appointed hour?
options: He opened the window vent and stared into the murky haze of thickly falling wet snow
He wrote a letter to Zverkov
He went out for a walk
reading.correct: He opened the window vent and stared into the murky haze of thickly falling wet snow
reading.explain: In inexpressible anguish he went to the window, opened the vent, and gazed into the murky haze of the thickly falling wet snow.
